concepts.name: Coral Polyp: Biology and Reef-Building Mechanism
key_dimensions: Structure of a coral polyp — exoskeleton (calcium carbonate) vs. soft tissue distinction
Symbiotic relationship with zooxanthellae algae and its role in reef building
Distinction between hermatypic (reef-building) and ahermatypic (non-reef-building) corals
Why corals are animals, not plants — a common UPSC trap

concepts.name: Conditions Required for Coral Reef Formation
key_dimensions: Temperature range (20–32°C) and why polar/deep-sea reefs are exceptions (cold-water corals)
Depth requirement (< 50m for photic zone) — sunlight dependency via zooxanthellae
Salinity, water clarity, and substrate requirements
UPSC trap: conditions that seem to allow reefs but don't (e.g., near river mouths — turbidity and low salinity)

concepts.name: Darwin's Theory of Coral Reef Formation (Subsidence Theory)
key_dimensions: Three-stage progression: fringing reef → barrier reef → atoll
Role of volcanic island subsidence and upward coral growth
Evidence supporting and challenging Darwin's theory (drilling evidence at Eniwetok Atoll)
Alternative theories: Daly's Glacial Control Theory — comparison and contrast with Darwin's

concepts.name: Fringing Reefs: Characteristics and Global Examples
key_dimensions: Definition — directly attached to or bordering a coastline with no lagoon or shallow lagoon
Distinction from barrier reefs — absence of deep, wide lagoon channel
Global examples: Red Sea coast, Florida Keys (partially), Andaman & Nicobar Islands (India)
UPSC trap: fringing reefs are the most common type — not barrier reefs or atolls

concepts.name: Barrier Reefs: Characteristics and the Great Barrier Reef
key_dimensions: Defining feature — separation from mainland by a deep, wide lagoon
Great Barrier Reef: location (Coral Sea, off Queensland, Australia), UNESCO status, size
Other examples: Belize Barrier Reef (second largest), New Caledonia Barrier Reef
UPSC trap: Great Barrier Reef is not a continuous wall — it is a system of ~2,900 individual reefs

concepts.name: Atolls: Formation, Structure, and Distribution
key_dimensions: Definition — ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a central lagoon, no central island
Exclusively found in tropical oceans, predominantly in the Pacific (Micronesia, Polynesia)
Indian Ocean examples: Lakshadweep Islands (India's only atolls), Maldives
UPSC trap: Lakshadweep islands are atolls; Andaman & Nicobar are not atolls — a frequent confusion point

concepts.name: Patch Reefs and Table Reefs: Lesser-Known Types
key_dimensions: Patch reefs — small, isolated reefs within a lagoon or on a continental shelf
Table reefs (platform reefs) — flat-topped reefs that do not enclose a lagoon
Distinction from atolls: table reefs lack a central lagoon
Relevance for MCQs where all four types are listed and the 'odd one out' is tested

concepts.name: Global Distribution Pattern of Coral Reefs
key_dimensions: Confined between 30°N and 30°S latitudes — the 'coral belt'
Concentration in Indo-Pacific region (holds ~75% of world's coral reefs)
Coral Triangle — location (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, PNG, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste) and biodiversity significance
Near-absence on western coasts of continents — cold currents (e.g., Peru Current, Benguela Current) as inhibiting factor

concepts.name: Coral Reefs in India: Types, Locations, and Legal Status
key_dimensions: Four major reef systems: Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Gulf of Kutch (fringing), Andaman & Nicobar (fringing), Lakshadweep (atolls)
Gulf of Mannar — India's first Marine Biosphere Reserve; fringing reef type
Gulf of Kutch — northernmost coral reefs of India; unique as they exist in higher turbidity
UPSC trap: Lakshadweep = atolls; Andaman & Nicobar = fringing reefs — not to be interchanged

concepts.name: Coral Bleaching: Causes, Process, and Consequences
key_dimensions: Mechanism — thermal stress causes expulsion of zooxanthellae, leading to white appearance
Triggers: sea surface temperature rise (even +1°C above mean for 4+ weeks), ocean acidification, pollution
Global Mass Bleaching Events — 1998, 2010, 2016 (most severe — linked to El Niño)
Distinction: bleaching ≠ death; recovery possible if stress is removed within weeks

concepts.name: Ocean Acidification and Its Impact on Coral Reefs
key_dimensions: Mechanism: increased CO₂ → carbonic acid → reduced carbonate ions → inhibits calcium carbonate skeleton formation
Impact on coral calcification rates and structural integrity of reefs
Synergistic effect with warming — dual threat concept
UPSC angle: how this links climate change (GS1 Geography) with environment policy (GS3)

concepts.name: Cold-Water (Deep-Sea) Coral Reefs: Exception to General Rules
key_dimensions: Exist at depths of 200–6,000m in cold waters — no dependency on zooxanthellae or sunlight
Found in North Atlantic (Norwegian fjords, Darwin Mounds off Scotland), Pacific, and Indian Oceans
Composed largely of Lophelia pertusa species
UPSC trap: 'Corals require warm, shallow, sunlit water' — cold-water corals are the critical exception

concepts.name: Coral Reef as an Ecosystem: Biodiversity and Services
key_dimensions: 'Rainforests of the Sea' — cover <1% of ocean floor but support ~25% of marine species
Ecosystem services: coastal protection (wave attenuation), fisheries, tourism, pharmaceutical potential
Trophic structure and keystone species (e.g., parrotfish, crown-of-thorns starfish as threat)
Economic valuation — reefs valued at $375 billion/year globally (World Bank figures for UPSC context)

concepts.name: Threats to Coral Reefs: Anthropogenic vs. Natural
key_dimensions: Anthropogenic: destructive fishing (blast fishing, cyanide fishing), coastal development, runoff/eutrophication, tourism
Natural threats: crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks, cyclones, predation
Sedimentation from deforestation and dredging — indirect anthropogenic threat
UPSC trap: distinguishing direct vs. indirect threats and matching them to specific reef systems in questions

concepts.name: Coral Triangle: Biodiversity Hotspot and Geopolitical Significance
key_dimensions: Location: six nations — Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste
Contains ~76% of known coral species and ~37% of world's reef fish species
CTI (Coral Triangle Initiative) — multilateral conservation framework
Overlap with South China Sea disputes — geopolitical dimension for GS2 integration

concepts.name: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and Coral Reef Bleaching
key_dimensions: El Niño events suppress upwelling, raise sea surface temperatures → triggers mass bleaching
1998 El Niño — killed ~16% of world's coral reefs in a single event
2016 event — worst recorded bleaching of Great Barrier Reef
La Niña as potential recovery window — nuanced understanding tested in mains

concepts.name: Reef Conservation Mechanisms: International and Indian Frameworks
key_dimensions: International: CITES (coral trade regulation), CBD (biodiversity targets), Ramsar (wetland overlap for some reefs)
India: Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (Schedule I protection for corals), Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) notifications
Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park and Biosphere Reserve — India's landmark reef protection
UPSC trap: Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) vs. Marine National Parks vs. Marine Biosphere Reserves — definitional distinctions

concepts.name: Coral Reef Restoration Techniques: Emerging Concepts
key_dimensions: Coral gardening / coral fragmentation and transplantation methods
Assisted evolution — breeding heat-resistant coral strains (relevance to GS3 science & technology)
Biorock/mineral accretion technology — using low-voltage electrical current to accelerate reef growth
UPSC mains angle: critically evaluate the effectiveness of restoration vs. addressing root causes

concepts.name: Relationship Between Coral Reefs and Mangroves/Seagrasses
key_dimensions: Trifecta ecosystem concept — coral reefs, mangroves, and seagrass beds as interdependent systems
Mangroves filter sediment and nutrients protecting adjacent reefs; seagrasses provide nursery habitat
Spatial distribution overlap — all three found in tropical coastal zones
UPSC trap: treating these as separate ecosystems when questions test their ecological linkages

concepts.name: Reefs and Sea Level Change: Paleoclimate and Future Projections
key_dimensions: Fossil reefs as paleoclimate indicators — past sea level and temperature reconstruction
Coral growth rate vs. projected sea level rise — 'keep-up, catch-up, or give-up' scenarios
Atoll nations (Maldives, Tuvalu, Kiribati) — existential threat framing for GS1 and GS2
UPSC mains angle: connecting sea level rise, reef health, and climate justice/UNFCCC negotiations
